system_description.narrative_title: China's expanding global reach reshaping trade, logistics and security
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that China is leveraging trade, shipping innovation, industrial policy and state tools (tax, regulation, cyber and military signalling) to extend economic and strategic influence worldwide. This is producing new logistics routes (Arctic 'Ice Silk Road'), surging exports that stress global supply chains, corporate relocations and political pushback, while prompting security and regulatory responses from other states and firms. The system is driven by flows (goods, capital, information), chokepoints, and governance levers rather than single events.
system_description.scope: China's external economic and strategic activities and their immediate global effects: export flows (especially autos and energy), alternative shipping routes and logistics infrastructure, state regulatory/tax actions, cyber and military signalling, multinational corporate responses and partner-state reactions.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical-economic order (international trade, global supply chains, and security architecture).
adjacent_subsystems: Global shipping and Arctic maritime routes
International technology, cyber and data governance
Regional security architecture in East Asia

variables.name: Export volume of manufactured goods
variables.description: Rate and value of manufactured goods shipped abroad per unit time.

variables.name: Maritime shipping capacity
variables.description: Total available ocean transport capacity measured in tonnage/TEU and vessel availability.

variables.name: Arctic route throughput
variables.description: Volume of cargo transiting Arctic sea routes per unit time.

variables.name: Supply chain resilience
variables.description: Overall ability of supply chains to absorb, adapt to, and recover from disruptions.

variables.name: Chokepoint congestion
variables.description: Degree of backlog and flow restriction at key maritime and logistics chokepoints.

variables.name: Regulatory and tax activism
variables.description: Intensity of cross-border use of regulations, taxes, and enforcement actions to achieve strategic aims.

variables.name: Tax policy aggressiveness
variables.description: Extent and frequency of assertive or retroactive tax measures deployed for economic objectives.

variables.name: Foreign investment flows
variables.description: Net rate of cross-border direct and portfolio investment moving into and out of jurisdictions.

variables.name: Technology transfer rate
variables.description: Rate at which industrial and technological capabilities diffuse across borders through trade, licensing, and investment.

variables.name: Hybrid security signal intensity
variables.description: Frequency and intensity of cyber, military, and other security signaling directed at external actors.

variables.name: Corporate relocation rate
variables.description: Rate at which firms shift production, supply relationships, or corporate presence across borders.

variables.name: Global freight rate level
variables.description: Average price level for moving goods across major maritime and multimodal routes.

variables.name: Supply chain geographic spread
variables.description: Degree of geographic dispersion of suppliers, production sites, and logistics nodes.

variables.name: External strategic threat perception
variables.description: Aggregate perception among foreign actors of the strategic threat posed by external economic and security actions.

variables.name: Port infrastructure capacity
variables.description: Aggregate handling capacity, berth availability, and hinterland links of port and terminal systems.

variables.name: Arctic navigability
variables.description: Seasonal and long-term environmental conditions affecting the viability of Arctic sea routes.

catalysts.title: Regular Arctic 'Ice Silk Road' cargo service expands
catalysts.description: Establishment and scaling of regular cargo sailings via Northern Sea Route ('Ice Silk Road'), creating a persistent alternative to traditional chokepoints.
catalysts.rationale: Reports of China opening the first regular Arctic cargo route and 'Ice Silk Road' expansion. [2026-08-15/16 FT, WSJ]

catalysts.title: Sustained surge in Chinese auto exports
catalysts.description: Continued rapid growth of Chinese vehicle exports strains shipping capacity, ports and raises freight rates while testing logistics networks.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: booming Chinese car exports and lack of ships; firms moving production (Ford) and China tightening control of car supply chains. [2026-08-14/15]

catalysts.title: Expanded Chinese global tax enforcement and retroactive claims
catalysts.description: Beijing's cross-border tax investigations and retroactive tax measures broaden, creating legal/regulatory uncertainty for foreign actors and firms.
catalysts.rationale: FT reports China launching a global tax hunt and Hong Kong tax reforms; Beijing clarifying rules stoking wealthy confusion. [2026-08-14/15]

catalysts.title: Intensifying cross-strait military and cyber signaling
catalysts.description: Renewed military drills, coast guard tactics, and AI-driven hacking campaigns increase security signaling and raise strategic risk perceptions.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Taiwan targeted by AI-driven hacking, annual drills, coast guard preparations and Chinese dismissals of drills. [2026-08-14/15]

catalysts.title: Resource competition and local resistance in lithium supply buildout
catalysts.description: Accelerated efforts to secure lithium capacity (US/China competition) face water-use conflicts and local opposition, slowing supply expansion.
catalysts.rationale: FT: US race with China on lithium 'runs into water battles', implying slowed/contested supply expansions. [2026-08-14]

catalysts.title: Greater global uptake of Chinese technology by multinationals
catalysts.description: Multinationals increasingly adopt Chinese tech and components, accelerating cross-border diffusion of capabilities and raising governance concerns.
catalysts.rationale: Articles note Chinese tech's growing influence on global companies and concerns about censorship and medicine supply dependencies. [2026-08-14]
